thread:
maria: Heads-up — I rolled a tighter egress policy on the privatelink/NAT stack last night to close an audit gap. Now seeing a spike of EU GPU nodes stuck in provisioning since ~03:20 UTC. Anyone else seeing keystore decrypt errors?

jon: Yep, saw the same. Warm-pool joins failing with `keystore decrypt timeout` and a bunch of 403s from the KMS proxy. Looks like the new deny blocked outbound to the central logging bucket in us-east-1.

sam: Pasted logs from a staging node: 
```
2026-03-20T03:21:12Z kubelet: keystore-decrypt failed: connect timeout to s3.amazonaws.com (blocked by sg-0a1b2c3d)
2026-03-20T03:22:05Z node-provision: vault:403 AccessDenied for kms:Decrypt
```

zoe: I had flagged the rule change in the PR — the intent was to stop unapproved cross-region egress, but we removed the S3 allowlist used by the keystore/logshipper. Compliance wanted central ingestion to be attested, so we tightened retention/replication earlier, but we forgot the service exception.

maria: Ok my bad on the rollback plan. I can revert the rule to unblock nodes, but that defeats the audit control. We need a narrow exception instead of a blunt revert.

jon: Reverting will definitely bring nodes back, but FYI it increases egress costs — we're replicating logs to us-east and retention went up to 30d. Last month that showed ~12% bump in S3 egress for EU.

zoe: Compliance is aware of the cost delta but prefers central logs for attestation. Proposed middle ground: targeted allowlist or role-based exception for the keystore service only.

sam: Suggestion: add an S3 bucket policy + NAT exception that only allows keystore uploads to `arn:aws:s3:::redwood-keystore-logs/*` and require calls signed by `role/keystore-service`. That keeps scope tight.

maria: Can we enforce that at the firewall level? Security groups can't check IAM role. We can tag ENIs and allow outbound from those tags in the privnet firewall, and enforce IAM at the S3/KMS layer.

jon: Another option — provision a VPC gateway endpoint for S3 in eu-west-1 so traffic stays in-region (no NAT), removing egress charges and simplifying policy. Downside: cross-region replication/KMS calls to us-east still need NAT/KMS reachability.

zoe: VPC endpoint is a good long-term fix. It also reduces audit surface. But we still need KMS cross-region decrypts for HSM-backed keys in us-east. Either replicate keys or proxy KMS calls (higher effort).

maria: Short-term plan: implement a targeted egress exception for ENIs tagged `keystore=true` to allow `s3.amazonaws.com` and `kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` for a small maintenance window. Then roll the endpoint + key replication RFC.

sam: I can push that patch. Note: our firewall supports tag-based rules. CLI snippet to add rule (staging):
```
privnetctl egress add --tag keystore=true --allow hosts:s3.amazonaws.com,kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com --duration 30m
```
I'll run canary first.

maria: deploy-bot: please start the canary for the tag-based egress exception.

deploy-bot: Rollout started by maria at 2026-03-20T03:40:00Z — canary nodes: 2/2 healthy. Applying egress exception for tag=`keystore=true` to allow `s3.amazonaws.com` and `kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` for 30 minutes.

zoe: Compliance: noted. We'll accept a 30m exception if there's a follow-up RFC + postmortem. Please attach the alerting group (sec-ops) and a timeline. :+1:

maria: Nodes are rejoining after the exception. Provisioning backlog clearing. I'll open an RFC for the longer term plan (endpoint + key replication or multi-region KMS).

sam: Created RFC placeholder: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/keystore-egress-multiregion (will flesh out replication cost vs endpoint ops). Estimated cost delta: ~+$1.2k/mo if we keep cross-region retention at 30d without gateway endpoints.

jon: Looping in @finance — can you weigh endpoint infra cost vs ongoing egress? Endpoint + key replication might be capex (engineering time) but saves monthly ops cost.

zoe: Adding to compliance board and will sign off once RFC includes KMS key replication plan and audit proof. Follow-up postmortem in #postmortems when RFC lands.

maria: Thanks all — rolling exception worked. I'll leave the temporary rule on for 30m and then remove it unless RFC lands earlier. Will post updates in this thread. :wave:
